rules.text: Posting year is the PSLE/S1 posting exercise year. S1 entry occurs the following year. The 2024 and 2025 values are historical inputs for planning 2027 entry, not confirmed 2027 cut-offs.
A student may submit up to six school/programme choices. Encourage use of all six where suitable, without labelling six as a mandatory minimum.
For an option-band student, one selected Posting Group applies to all submitted choices. Do not mix PG2 and PG3, or PG1 and PG2, within one submitted list.

Use current official admission eligibility to determine selectable schools. A score worse than a historical COP is a comparison result, not a reason by itself to prohibit selecting the school. Historical data does not supply admission probabilities.

At a dual-track school, IP and SEC are separate choices with different programme choice codes. Retain both routes. When validating duplicates, use selected Posting Group plus programme choice code, rather than school identity alone.

Apply affiliated comparisons only when the pupil has the qualifying primary-school affiliation, meets any additional criteria and uses the required choice order. Normally the school must be first. The same dual-track school IP first and SEC second preserves SEC affiliation priority.

The six dual-track affiliated IP placeholders mean affiliation is inapplicable. Nanyang Girls has an actual affiliated IP range. Use the records and rule context instead of a universal IP-affiliation assumption.

At SAP schools, Higher Chinese priority applies to students with PSLE total 14 or better and a qualifying D, M or P grade, among students with the same total. Better total scores come first. The HCL priority order is D, M, P, then no qualifying HCL grade. Do not apply HCL priority above total 14 or convert HCL grades into AL bonus points. Preserve unknown student HCL status separately from no qualifying grade.
Verify current SAP admission conditions, including having taken English and Chinese at PSLE. HCL is not itself compulsory for SAP application; qualifying HCL priority applies for eligible scores.
After the applicable score and HCL considerations, ordinary tie-breakers are citizenship, choice order and computerised balloting. Matching a historical COP is not guaranteed admission.

A student successfully allocated to a school through DSA-Sec does not submit ordinary S1 school choices. Distinguish successful allocation from merely having made a DSA application or received an earlier offer.

When both years contain numeric COPs for the relevant route and affiliation, an optional two-year AL buffer is min(COP2024, COP2025) minus the student AL total. A positive number means a better total than both published COPs. Preserve HCL and vacancy flags separately. With either year absent, return null rather than a made-up two-year buffer.

Encourage at least two to three choices whose historical COPs are less stringent than the student score. Describe a positive historical buffer accurately; avoid guaranteed-admission or probability labels derived from two cut-offs.

Help the family order eligible choices by genuine preference, including curriculum fit, interests and travel. Recalculate the applicable affiliation category when choices are reordered. Do not silently sort the final list solely by COP.

The latest two released O-Level examination cohorts as of 24 November 2026 are 2024 and 2025, released in January 2025 and January 2026. Do not relabel January 2026 results as the 2026 examination cohort.

The SEC replaces N(T), N(A) and O-Level qualifications from 2027. Historical O-Level outcomes provide context for a 2027 entrant; they do not predict that child’s eventual SEC results. IP and specialised routes must be described separately.
Display an explicit result status for every school/year. Null or absent results must never become zero, a fail, a poor-school label or a negative score.

Compare only like examination year, cohort, metric, threshold, aggregation and raw/net definition. Five passes, five distinctions, JC eligibility, JC/MI eligibility, poly eligibility and eligibility for any post-secondary institution are different measures.

Published outcomes mix incoming student differences, cohort composition and many other influences. They do not estimate a school’s causal contribution. The cut-off and O-Level cohorts in this file are also different groups of students.
Show a programme or CCA as a documented opportunity. Show selection, route, gender, year, capacity and timetable limitations separately; never promise a place from a directory entry.
Present the published fact, the student-value interpretation and the family’s own fit assessment as separate fields. A long programme list is not a quality score.
Preserve school_id through renaming and relocation. Use the campus for the intended intake when calculating travel, and flag old-cohort examination results after a campus move or merger.

Use existing eligibility and affiliation rules, then help the student compare interests, support, travel, costs and pathway fit. Historical outcomes are one context field, with disclosure quality shown separately. Do not create an admissions probability or universal school ranking.
